raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Closes #50356

Add OpenAI-compatible `verbose_json` responses to `/v1/audio/transcriptions` for `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`. MOSS emits a canonical `[start][Sxx]text[end]` transcript, whereas the existing verbose path expects Whisper timestamp tokens. This change adds the small model capability required to parse MOSS's textual timestamps, preserve
the generated token IDs and log probabilities per segment, and retain the existing Whisper path unchanged.

The OpenAI verbose-transcription schema has no `speaker` field. Therefore, speaker labels are preserved in `text` as `[S01]...`, both per segment and in the aggregate transcript, rather than being discarded or adding a
non-standard response field.

The OpenAI-compatible verbose response schema requires a non-null [`language`](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/audio/subresources/transcriptions/methods/create#(resource)%20audio.transcriptions%20%3E%20(model)%20transcription_verbose%20%3E%20(schema)%20%3E%20(property)%20language) field. MOSS accepts a language hint but does not expose language identification. The supplied request language is returned; when it is absent, the response uses `"unknown"` rather than emitting `null`. Returning `null` would violate the response contract and can break strongly typed OpenAI clients.

MOSS only produces segment-level timestamps. As with the existing endpoint behavior, `timestamp_granularities[]=word` is accepted but does not synthesize word timestamps.

## Test Plan

### Automated tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/moss_transcribe_diarize.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/base/serving.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/moss_transcribe_diarize.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_inter_chunk_spacing.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_moss_transcribe_diarize.py

git diff --check
```

The tests cover MOSS's textual timestamp parsing and token/logprob attribution, fail-closed behavior when token text cannot reconstruct the model output, the decoder-only prompt path, and response construction without a language hint.

### Local end-to-end validation

Sent requests to a local vLLM server using:

- Model: `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`
- Audio: [AMI Meeting Corpus](https://groups.inf.ed.ac.uk/ami/corpus/) `ES2002a.Mix-Headset.wav`, recut to a 90-second mono, 16 kHz WAV
- Request parameters: `language=en`, `temperature=0`
- Hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 5600 and AMD Radeon RX 7700 XT
- Runtime: ROCm 7.2.4
- Serving configuration: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-model-len 20000`

After one excluded warm-up per format, five sequential alternating `json` and `verbose_json` requests were issued. Every verbose response returned HTTP 200, 26 non-empty speaker-prefixed segments, non-empty token arrays, valid `start <= end` timestamps, and top-level `text` equal to the space-joined segment text. Additional `verbose_json` requests without `language` and with `timestamp_granularities[]=word` both returned HTTP 200; the former returned `language: "unknown"` and the latter returned no synthetic `words` entries.

## Test Result

### Automated

```text
34 passed
ruff-check: passed
mypy-3.12: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

### End-to-end API result

```jsonc
{
  "duration": 90.0,
  "language": "en",
  "text": "[S01]Um. [S02]My gosh, you've already pris- produced a PowerPoint presentation. ...",
  "segments": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "start": 0.0,
      "end": 0.82,
      "text": "[S01]Um.",
      "tokens": [58, 15, 13, 15, 15, 60, 42474, 15, 16, 60, 23334, 7873, 15, 13, 23, 17, 1457],
      "avg_logprob": -0.10790063205954974
    }
    // ... 25 additional segments
  ]
}
```

### Parser cost

On the captured MOSS transcript (1,215 characters, 602 tokens, 26 segments), seven samples of 10,000 `parse_verbose_transcript` calls, including token-to-segment association, measured:

```text
median: 0.214270 ms per parse
min:    0.212515 ms per parse
max:    0.220118 ms per parse
```

### Client-observed end-to-end latency

Times include request handling, inference, verbose logprob collection, parsing, and serialization. Warm-ups are excluded.

Run | `json` (s) | `verbose_json` (s)
--- | ---: | ---:
1 | 4.673524 | 4.820702
2 | 4.681948 | 4.820337
3 | 4.673798 | 4.814655
4 | 4.668837 | 4.816914
5 | 4.672164 | 4.816530
Mean | 4.674054 | 4.817828
Median | 4.673524 | 4.816914

The mean end-to-end difference is `+0.143773 s` (`+3.08%`). This includes verbose-only logprob collection and the larger response payload; the isolated MOSS parser cost is 0.214 ms per response.

---

<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

nodes.body: Thanks! I'm a bit confused why did `verbose_json` take more time than `json`?

@gcanlin
Thanks for pointing this out

In the existing `verbose_json` serving path, vLLM sets `logprobs=1` for the generation, then builds a response segment for each timestamped span, this may require retaining each generated token's decoded text and logprob, computing
segment metadata, and serializing the resulting token arrays, the plain `json` path does none of that and only returns the final text

To check that this was not a regression introduced by the changes i made in MOSS, I also repeated the same five sequential `json`/`verbose_json` pairs with whisper-large-v3 on the same audio. Whisper showed a very similar relative difference with +3.37%

I revalidated this existing contribution because FunASR 1.4.8 now consumes vLLM's MOSS transcription contracts.

Exact compatibility evidence:

- PR commit `32f31188851804f41e5a2ffaa75e9b0d32678f29` applies cleanly, without conflict, to current vLLM `main@b383e163961650c663ad2062544ecbee1b56afc8` (1,253 commits newer than the PR base).
- The two declared focused suites execute fully on Python 3.12 / Transformers 5.15.0: **34 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` pass for all five changed files.
- The repository Mypy wrapper reports seven errors in two pre-existing paths, but a clean current-main worktree reports the identical seven errors at the corresponding pre-patch lines. This patch adds no Mypy delta.

The current red `pre-run-check` is policy-only: its log says the author has two merged PRs and the branch lacks `ready`, `ready-run-all-tests`, or `verified`, so pre-commit is intentionally skipped.

@gcanlin, if this `verbose_json` capability is still desired, could you add the appropriate ready/verified label so the repository CI can run on the author's branch? I have not pushed to or replaced the contributor's PR.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @wskr00.

issue_comments.body: Thanks! I'm a bit confused why did `verbose_json` take more time than `json`?

@gcanlin
Thanks for pointing this out

In the existing `verbose_json` serving path, vLLM sets `logprobs=1` for the generation, then builds a response segment for each timestamped span, this may require retaining each generated token's decoded text and logprob, computing
segment metadata, and serializing the resulting token arrays, the plain `json` path does none of that and only returns the final text

To check that this was not a regression introduced by the changes i made in MOSS, I also repeated the same five sequential `json`/`verbose_json` pairs with whisper-large-v3 on the same audio. Whisper showed a very similar relative difference with +3.37%

I revalidated this existing contribution because FunASR 1.4.8 now consumes vLLM's MOSS transcription contracts.

Exact compatibility evidence:

- PR commit `32f31188851804f41e5a2ffaa75e9b0d32678f29` applies cleanly, without conflict, to current vLLM `main@b383e163961650c663ad2062544ecbee1b56afc8` (1,253 commits newer than the PR base).
- The two declared focused suites execute fully on Python 3.12 / Transformers 5.15.0: **34 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` pass for all five changed files.
- The repository Mypy wrapper reports seven errors in two pre-existing paths, but a clean current-main worktree reports the identical seven errors at the corresponding pre-patch lines. This patch adds no Mypy delta.

The current red `pre-run-check` is policy-only: its log says the author has two merged PRs and the branch lacks `ready`, `ready-run-all-tests`, or `verified`, so pre-commit is intentionally skipped.

@gcanlin, if this `verbose_json` capability is still desired, could you add the appropriate ready/verified label so the repository CI can run on the author's branch? I have not pushed to or replaced the contributor's PR.
